title: Urinary extracellular vesicle analysis and detection of low abundance immunoglobulin oligomers in samples isolated from patients with significant urine proteinuria
protocol: Obtain clinical residual urine taken from 24 hour urine collections of plasma cell dyscrasia patients.
Supplement urine samples with 10% sodium azide preservative to a final concentration of 0.02% (1:50 dilution).
Store the urine samples at 4°C until further processing.
Obtain control urine sample from a healthy volunteer.
Preserve and store the control urine in the same manner as patient samples.
Dispense 4L purified H2O into an appropriately-sized beaker and add a magnetic stir bar.
Cut an 8 inch length of dialysis tubing (Spectra/Por #132725 3.5 kD MWCO) and pre-wet the membrane in H2O.
Secure a dialysis clip to one end of the tubing, then loosen the opposite end of the tubing with a gloved hand to open.
Dispense 100 ml urine into the open end of the dialysis tubing using a 50 ml serological pipet.
Secure the open end of the tubing with a dialysis clip, leaving a small amount of air over the top of the urine sample.
Position a foam float onto the top dialysis clip.
Deposit the urine-filled dialysis tubing into the beaker containing 4L purified H2O.
Cover the beaker with aluminum foil, place the beaker on a magnetic stirrer and dialyze the sample overnight at 4°C.
After dialysis, remove the dialyzed urine sample from the beaker and rinse the membrane with H2O.
Gently remove the foam float and top clip from the dialysis tubing, ensuring not to spill the urine sample.
Pour the urine into a 250 ml 0.2 micron filtration unit and apply a vacuum to filter the sample.
After filtration, add 10% sodium azide to a final concentration of 0.02%.
Add ½ protease inhibitor tablet to the filtered urine sample.
Pre-cool an ultracentrifuge and Ti70 rotor to 4°C.
Dispense urine sample into paired 29.9 ml Optiseal tubes with a 25 ml serological pipet.
Balance the tubes in opposite pairs using 1X PBS.
Seal the tubes by inserting the vendor-supplied plug seals.
Load the tubes into the pre-cooled Ti70 rotor.
Insert tube spacers, ensuring they are fully seated over the Optiseal tubes, and secure the rotor cover.
Centrifuge the samples at 100,000 x g for 90 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the tube spacers using a threaded spacer removal tool.
Remove the Optiseal tubes from the rotor using an extraction tool.
Remove the plug seals from the tubes using forceps.
Remove and discard about one-third of the urine sample volume from the tube using a disposable plastic bulb transfer pipet.
Carefully remove the top of the tube by cutting with a razor blade.
Pour off the remainder of the sample into a collection beaker and dab any remaining liquid onto a paper towel.
Place the tube on ice for the remainder of the processing steps.
Add 375 μl storage solution to one tube of each pair.
Seal the top of the tube with parafilm and vortex on maximum speed for 45 seconds.
Transfer the liquid resuspension from the first to the second tube of each pair.
Repeat the vortex step.
Transfer the contents of both tubes into a 2 ml screw-cap microtube.
Label the microtubes appropriately.
Store vesicle stocks at 4°C for immediate use.
Store vesicle stocks at -80°C for long-term preservation if needed.
Prepare Transfer Buffer solution at least 24 hours prior to use.
Add 400 mL of methanol (MeOH) to a 4L beaker.
Add 600 mL of nanopure water to the beaker.
Weigh and add 57.7 g of glycine to the beaker.
Mix the solution thoroughly.
Weigh and add 12.0 g TRIZMA Base to the beaker.
Mix until all solids have dissolved (add nanopure water if necessary).
Add solution to 2 L graduated cylinder and adjust volume to 2 L with nanopure water.
Pour the adjusted solution into 2 L bottles.
Add 1 mL of 20% SDS solution to achieve a 1:2000 dilution.
Mix well, watching for foam formation.
Store in the refrigerator at 4°C until use.
Weigh 292.2 g of NaCl and add to a 1L beaker.
Add 500 mL nanopure water to the beaker and allow the solution to mix.
Slowly add nanopure water to the 900 mL mark on the beaker and mix thoroughly.
Empty the contents of the beaker into a 1 L graduated cylinder.
Bring the volume to 1 L with nanopure water.
Pour the solution into 1 L or 2 x 500 mL bottles.
Store at room temperature.
Add 100 mL wash buffer to a 200 mL beaker.
Weigh and add 4 g of albumin to the 100 mL wash buffer.
Mix the solution completely on a stir-plate to ensure all the albumin has gone into solution.
Mix the blocking buffer during the transfer step or prepare a stock solution with 0.01% sodium azide and store at 4°C.
Add the blocking buffer to membranes without pouring directly onto them.
Add 100 mL of 10X Tris/Glycine/SDS Buffer to a 1000mL graduated cylinder.
Add 900 mL nanopure water to the 1000 mL graduated cylinder.
Place Parafilm over the mouth of the graduate cylinder and invert to mix.
Store the mixed buffer at room temperature for future use.
Prepare in a fume hood due to toxic fumes from beta-mercaptoethanol.
Add 15 ml purified water to a 50 ml graduated cylinder.
Add 6.25 ml 1M Tris-HCl pH 6.8.
Add 200 µl Beta-mercaptoethanol.
Add 10 ml 20% SDS solution.
Add 10 ml Glycerol.
Add 30 mg Bromophenol Blue powder.
Bring to final volume of 50 ml with purified water.
Determine uEV protein concentration and calculate required sample amount for assay detection limit.
Vortex the uEV sample prior to pipetting it.
Mix the uEV sample protein in a 1:1 ratio with 2X SDS Loading Dye by pipetting the mixture up and down.
Heat sample(s) at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Unwrap the Criterion Precast Gel (4-15% Gradient; 18-well; 30µL/well).
Remove gel from plastic dish.
Remove the tape at the bottom of the Criterion gel.
Place the Criterion gel into the Criterion electrophoresis cell.
Fill the Criterion gel box to the fill-line with 1X Tris/Glycine/SDS Buffer (TGS).
Fill the top of the Criterion gel with 1X Tris/Glycine/SDS Buffer.
Remove the well comb from the Criterion gel.
Load 20 µL of the ladder into the first well of the Criterion gel.
Load 20 µL of sample into separate wells in the Criterion gel.
Add 20 µL of 2X SDS Loading Dye to empty wells.
Run the gel at 100 volts.
Continue running until the blue dye front reaches the bottom of the gel and then turn off.
Fill the Criterion transfer box with cold transfer buffer.
Cut a piece of Immobilon-P Transfer Membrane the size of the running gel.
Label membrane in a corner with a methanol-proof marker or pencil to maintain orientation during processing.
Remove the Criterion gel from the Criterion electrophoresis cell.
Remove the Criterion gel from the plastic running cassette.
Break seal with spatula and watch for flying debris.
Place the gel in a plastic dish containing cold transfer buffer to rinse for about 5 minutes.
Fill the Pyrex dish with cold transfer buffer.
Open the transfer cassette and place the negative side flat in a Pyrex dish.
Wet one cassette sponge with cold transfer buffer and place it on the negative side of the open cassette.
Wet one piece of Blotter paper in cold transfer buffer and place it on top of the sponge.
Place the gel on top of the Blotter paper.
Make sure all air bubbles are removed from underneath the gel.
Place the membrane in a plastic dish containing methanol for 30 to 60 seconds to activate.
Rinse the activated membrane in cold transfer buffer.
Place the membrane on the gel (ensure there are no air bubbles).
Gently smooth over the membrane with the back of finger to help remove any air bubbles.
Place a piece of wet Blotter paper, soaked in cold transfer buffer, over the membrane.
Roll the bubbles out of the membrane/gel sandwich using a broken serological pipette.
Place the second cassette sponge, soaked in cold transfer buffer, on top of the Blotter paper.
Close the cassette (positive side over membrane, negative side under gel).
Place the transfer cassette in the Transfer box with the membrane facing you.
Add an ice pack to the back of the Transfer box. Close latch over cold pack.
Transfer at 100V for 60 minutes.
Remove transfer cassette from the Transfer box after completion.
Open transfer cassette with POSITIVE side up and remove the top piece of filter/blotter paper.
Mark the bands of the ladder on the membrane using a Fisher marker.
Rinse the membrane 2x with MilliQ water to remove excess marker without running water directly on membrane.
Pour off final rinse and add blocking buffer to the PVDF transfer membrane (DO NOT pour directly on membrane).
Cover plastic dish securely with lid.
Place dish on the shaker in the cold room.
Adjust the shaker speed to prevent splashing of the blocking buffer.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Proceed to the Antibody Pre-incubation step the next morning.
Prepare a 1:10,000 dilution of sheep anti-Kappa free light chain antibody in wash buffer.
Dilute 1:20,000 Abcam rabbit anti-sheep pre-adsorbed secondary antibody in wash buffer.
Incubate the tube on the membrane rocker for 2 hours at room temperature.
Hand mix the solution periodically every 20 minutes.
Prepare the membrane for blotting when incubation is 5 minutes from completion.
Remove blocking buffer and store it at 4°C for reuse.
Do not re-use more than 3 times.
Transfer the membrane to a clean container.
Wash the membrane at least twice with wash buffer.
Add the antibody mixture to the transfer membrane without pouring directly on it.
Incubate for 2 hours at room temperature on the shaker.
Wash twice for 5 minutes and then three times for 20 minutes each with wash buffer.
Place a sheet of plastic wrap on the bench-top.
Prepare ECL Developing reagents at a 1:1 ratio according to package directions.
Add 6.0 mL of the solution in the white bottle to the 15 mL conical tube.
Add 6.0 mL of the solution in the black bottle to the 15 mL conical tube.
Mix the 15 mL conical tube by inverting.
Transfer PVDF membrane to a clean plastic dish.
Pour the ECL solution into the dish.
Agitate the ECL solution over the membrane for 5 minutes.
Remove the blot from the ECL solution.
Gently dab the corner of the membrane to remove excess ECL.
Place the blot on plastic wrap with the protein side down.
Wrap the blot in plastic wrap and transfer it to a film cassette.
Tape the outer edges of the blot to keep it in place during transport.
Go to the dark room.
Open the cassette in the dark room with safety light on.
Place one piece of film on top of the blot, aligning the film edge with the bottom left corner of the cassette.
Close cassette lid.
Start timer for desired exposure time.
After the desired exposure time has finished, open cassette.
Gently remove film and immediately feed into the Exomat.
Once the Exomat develops the film, label the film with exposure time, date, primary used, secondary used and developer used.
Also, label all steps of the ladder as seen on the blot.
Mark the ladder locations on the plastic wrap surrounding the blot with a small black dot.
Repeat steps 3-7 for differing exposure times.
Take exposures at 1, 5, 30, and 60 minutes before exposing overnight.
Use the longest exposure that contains a negative control sample for interpretation of bands above 250kDa.
Label films immediately with exposure time, antibody concentrations, and incubation conditions.
When you get all the exposures you need and you are finished with the membrane, store transfer membrane wrapped in a refrigerator.
